key_insight: Retrieval is the main bottleneck in biomedical claim verification: valid PubMed IDs can still point to irrelevant papers.
engineering_relevance: Scientific-agent harnesses should enable model-written search queries and validate citation relevance, not merely identifier existence.
method: Evaluate SciFact claim verification with live PubMed as the only tool.
Compare closed-book, claim-as-query retrieval, ReAct-style search, and gold-abstract oracle harnesses.
Hold output format fixed and test each harness with two efficient frontier backbones.
evidence_signal: Agent-written queries tripled gold-paper recall over naive retrieval and achieved 62% verdict accuracy; gold abstracts raised accuracy to 79–86%, while only 3 of 327 existing closed-book citations were judged relevant.
watch_item: Accuracy differences among realistic harnesses were not statistically significant at this sample size, and agents used less than half their search budget.
paper_title: Real PMIDs, Wrong Papers: Harness Design for Biomedical Claim-Verification Agents
